claude_take: The common thread today is oversight working only when someone specific chooses to use it. Trump's promise of an "AI Force" and a soon-to-be-named czar is long on gesture and short on substance -- it does nothing about Plugin4Shell, a real zero-click flaw in AI coding agents that Google has simply decided it will never patch. Meanwhile the actual friction is coming from individuals willing to hold a line alone: a federal judge refusing to rubber-stamp TikTok's child-privacy settlement, and a handful of state attorneys general breaking from their own coalition rather than wave through a negotiated Paramount-Warner Bros. deal. It's a strange contrast with fashion's own watchdog, whose president resigned this week after physically overpowering the protester his organization exists to make room for -- a reminder that the people meant to hold institutions accountable are just as capable of becoming the problem.
claude_take_title: Oversight Is Only As Real As Who Uses It

items.headline: Trump Announces 'AI Force' and Plans to Name an AI Czar
items.summary: In a lengthy Truth Social post, President Trump said he would form an "AI Force" modeled on the Space Force and soon appoint an AI "czar" to lead it, framing the move as protecting the AI industry from being "destroyed" by proposed restrictions. The announcement came days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publicly called for pacing frontier AI development, a proposal Trump is effectively rejecting even as he moves to keep the government involved in the industry's growth. He offered no detail on the czar's authority or structure, joking only that "only high I.Q. individuals need apply."

items.headline: Zero-Click Flaw Exposes Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Gemini CLI to Takeover
items.summary: Security researchers disclosed Plugin4Shell, a zero-click remote-code-execution flaw rooted in a shared assumption across four major AI coding agents: each checks that a plugin update matches a pinned commit hash but never verifies the hash actually resolves to the expected code, letting an attacker who controls a plugin's repo slip in malicious code that still reports as verified. Anthropic patched Claude Code and OpenAI patched Codex soon after disclosure, but Microsoft has not yet fixed GitHub Copilot, and Google says it will not patch the deprecated Gemini CLI at all, leaving those installs permanently exposed. Because these plugins typically inherit a developer's full permissions, including cloud credentials and production access, the flaw underscores how much trust agentic coding tools now hold with too little verification behind it.

items.headline: 'La Bola Negra' Wins Toronto Film Festival's People's Choice Award
items.summary: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi's Spanish drama "La Bola Negra" won the People's Choice Award at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, historically one of the strongest Oscar-season bellwethers on the festival circuit. Peter Farrelly's "I Play Rocky" and Sian Heder's opening-night film "Being Heumann" were the first and second runners-up, while Simon Stone's "Elsinore" took the International People's Choice prize. The wins cap a festival that also launched TIFF's first official industry content market alongside its public program.

items.headline: State AGs Split Over Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Settlement Talks
items.summary: Paramount Skydance is in advanced settlement talks with California Attorney General Rob Bonta over the antitrust suit blocking its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, but the 12-state coalition that filed the suit is fracturing over the terms. New York's Letitia James is pushing for stronger worker protections and Connecticut's William Tong wants guarantees preserving CNN and CBS News' editorial independence, while other holdout states argue any settlement is a capitulation on a merger they say should be blocked outright. The split leaves the fate of one of the year's biggest media mergers in the hands of attorneys general who no longer agree on how hard to fight it.

items.headline: San Sebastian Opens With Donostia Awards for Werner Herzog and Naomi Watts
items.summary: The 74th San Sebastian Film Festival opened with a lifetime-achievement Donostia Award for Werner Herzog, followed a day later by one for Naomi Watts, who dedicated hers to her late "Mulholland Drive" director David Lynch and used her speech to criticize Hollywood's ageism toward actresses. The honors place both alongside a Donostia roll call that includes Gregory Peck, Bette Davis and Pedro Almodovar, underscoring the festival's standing as a prestige stop on the fall circuit alongside Venice, Telluride and Toronto. The festival runs through September 26, with Brad Pitt and Penelope Cruz also among its Oscar-season attendees.

items.headline: Judge Rejects Part of TikTok's $400 Million Child-Privacy Settlement
items.summary: A federal judge in Los Angeles tentatively refused to lift oversight obligations tied to TikTok's predecessor Musical.ly as part of a $400 million settlement TikTok and the Justice Department struck last month over children's privacy violations. US District Judge George Wu said neither TikTok nor the government had shown why the original court order protecting users under 13 should be vacated, meaning the company stays under active judicial monitoring rather than closing the case as planned. The ruling complicates one of the largest child-privacy settlements ever reached with a social platform and signals judges may be less willing to rubber-stamp negotiated tech settlements going forward.

items.headline: CFDA President Steven Kolb Resigns After PETA Altercation
items.summary: Steven Kolb stepped down as president and CEO of the Council of Fashion Designers of America after two decades in the role, days after video showed him physically restraining and covering the mouth of a PETA protester demonstrating against wool use at a New York Fashion Week show. Kolb had apologized and taken a leave of absence before announcing his resignation; PETA said it would not press charges and still hopes to meet with him about ending the industry's use of animal skins and wool. The abrupt exit removes one of American fashion's most visible institutional leaders just as the industry heads into Milan and Paris fashion weeks.

items.headline: Marx's Theory of Alienation
items.summary: Karl Marx argued that under capitalism, workers become alienated in four interlocking ways: from the products they make, from the act of labor itself, from their own human potential, and from other people, because production is organized around profit for owners rather than the needs or creativity of the people doing the work. Even when workers are paid fairly, Marx held, the structure of wage labor turns their activity into something done for someone else's benefit and stripped of intrinsic meaning. The concept remains a touchstone in debates about gig work, automation and burnout, offering a vocabulary for the sense that modern work can feel disconnected from any larger purpose even when it is not exploitative in a narrow legal sense.
items.summary_fr: Karl Marx soutenait que sous le capitalisme, le travailleur s'aliène de quatre manières indissociables : du produit de son travail, de l'acte même de travailler, de son potentiel proprement humain, et des autres, parce que la production est organisée autour du profit des propriétaires plutôt que des besoins ou de la créativité de ceux qui produisent. Même lorsque le salaire est juste, affirmait Marx, la structure du travail salarié transforme l'activité humaine en une tâche accomplie pour le bénéfice d'autrui, vidée de tout sens intrinsèque. Le concept reste une référence incontournable dans les débats sur le travail précaire, l'automatisation et l'épuisement professionnel, offrant un vocabulaire pour décrire cette sensation que le travail moderne peut sembler coupé de tout but supérieur, même sans exploitation flagrante au sens strict.
